<h1>Step values</h1>

The step views are where you shape the *relationship* between your steps: how much
velocity the trig on each step has, and how long or short the note it fires is. You draw
that shape once on the grid, and then that view's knob on the LaunchControl scales the
whole thing at once, louder or quieter, longer or shorter, without flattening the
sequence you programmed.

There are three of them. Two sit on the synth sequencers, one for **velocity** and one
for **duty**. The third is on the TR-8, for **accent**.

To edit, press any pad on the grid: the column picks the step, the row sets the value,
and the write happens straight away with no modifier held. The columns shaded slate grey
are the steps that carry a trig.

Holding SHIFT and pressing MUTE resets all sixteen steps to the level of the row you
press, and holding SHIFT and pressing SOLO randomises them around it.
[Reset and randomise](/documentation/MSEQ/reset) has the full matrix.

---

## What a value means

Every step holds a value from 0 to 7, and that number is never the velocity or the note
length the MSEQ sends. What it means depends on which view you are in, because the three views
measure three different things. The value in bold is the neutral one.

| Value | Duty (note length) | Velocity (share of the knob) | Accent (multiplier) |
|-------|--------------------|------------------------------|---------------------|
| 0 (bottom) | `1/64` | 8% | 0.80x |
| 1 | `1/32` | 14% | 0.85x |
| 2 | `1/16T` | 29% | 0.95x |
| 3 | `1/32.` | 43% | **1.00x** |
| 4 | **`1/16`** | 57% | 1.05x |
| 5 | `1/8T` | 71% | 1.10x |
| 6 | `1/16.` | 86% | 1.15x |
| 7 (top) | `1/8` | **100%** | 1.20x |

A value of 0 is never silence. On velocity it is the quietest value the MSEQ sends, and on duty
it is the shortest note rather than no note. To stop a step firing, turn its trig off.

---

## What acts on it

For the velocity and duty step views, the duty knob (top row) and velocity knob (middle
row) on the LaunchControl, in that sequencer's column, scale the value you set on the
grid.

The TR-8 accent is a velocity modifier across the whole kit. A synth row carries its own
velocity, but the TR-8 holds one accent value per step, shared by every voice, so it
lifts or drops everything firing on that step together. That is the 0.80x to 1.20x in
the table. The top knob row of its column sets how much of that spread applies, so with
it turned down the accent values stop doing anything.

<label for="tr8-accent-hardware">hardware</label>
<img class="shot-webapp" src="/assets/mseq/tr8-accent.png" alt="A TR-8 accent grid: most steps show a mustard pad at height 3, steps 3 and 11 sit higher in orange, steps 1 and 16 higher again in dark red, and nine of the sixteen columns are shaded slate behind the contour">
<img class="shot-hardware" src="/assets/mseq/hardware/tr8-accent.jpg" alt="A TR-8 accent grid: most steps show a mustard pad at height 3, steps 3 and 11 sit higher in orange, steps 1 and 16 higher again in dark red, and nine of the sixteen columns are shaded slate behind the contour, photographed on the hardware">
</figure>

*TR-8 accent on a busy kit. A baseline of 3, lifted to 5 on steps 3 and 11 and to 6 at
each end. Nine columns are slate, because on a drum pattern most steps carry a trig
somewhere.*

Arps act on your shape as well, and the two kinds act differently. A velo arp scales the
value you set, the same way the velocity knob does. A velo arp set to zero is the one
place a zero does silence a step, as a real rest. A duty arp does not scale at all: for
as long as it runs, its value *replaces* the per-step value on that row.
[Velo and duty arps](/documentation/MSEQ/velo-duty-arps) covers both.

The duty and velocity curves are per sequencer and you can edit them, so those two
columns show the shipped defaults. The accent spread is fixed. See
[Arp curves](/documentation/MSEQ/arp-curves).
